items.title: Alex Bigard Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: I went to go to Havana and see Miss Anna Keller. Anna Keller, yeah. Anna Keller was her name. And I got over there, I was a little too late for the job. She had got an officer from New York.

ctx.x: Yeah, he's all yeah. Yeah. I suppose when you came to him and you hadn't practiced your lesson, what would he do?

Well, he wouldn't do you anything if this youth was out of half a dollar, that's all. He's all he's making the money, he didn't care, but I mean he'd punish you and tell you, well I'm going to give you two lessons for one. He'd give you that lesson over again and give you another lesson. He'd say, now you bring those two lessons to me. He was a really wonderful, wonderful teacher. I'll tell you another one that taught me plenty too, Professor Manmanetta. Oh yeah. When did you work with him? Well, I went away with…

When you played with that band, were they playing the same type of music that you'd been playing in New Orleans? I mean the same type of music? Oh yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. Was it a reading band? Yeah, it was all readings.
